newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares close at new record above 4,000.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares close at new record above 4,000.

text.p: 1440 GMT - The Swiss bourse closed firmer on broad front with the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) closing over 4,000 points for the first time.
The rise was due to technical factors, favourable bond markets, firming European bourses and strong advances in Roche certificates and major banks, a dealer said.
"We had a very active day and we remain very optimistic for the next two weeks," a trader noted, adding by month's end investors may turn wary ahead of February's FOMC meeting.
* The SMI was up 0.69 percent, or 27.5 points, to 4,007.1.
The SMI posted a new intra-day high of 4,009.2 points.
* All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) soared 17.10 points, or 0.67 percent, to 2,568.85 points.
Dealers said some of the moves were incidental as investors squared positions ahead of Friday's expiry on options and futures exchange Soffex.

* Roche certificates, which led the active list, powered ahead 135 francs to close on a new all-time high of 10,985 francs. The company reported 1996 sales rose 11 percent to 15.96 billion francs, beating expectations of around 15.8 billion.

* Banks, which have been under pressure recently due to concerns about accounts of Holocaust victims, reportedly gained ground on easing tensions between Switzerland and Jewish organisations. CS Group stood out with a jump of 3.50 francs, or 2.61 percent, to 137.75 francs.

* UBS bearer shares added nine francs to 1,155. After the bourse close, Standard & Poor's said it downgraded UBS's long-term rating to double-A-plus from triple-A. UBS has been on S&P's CreditWatch list since November after forecasting a loss of around 500 million francs due to extraordinary provisions.
* Dollar-sensitive ABB, Alusuisse and SMH saw good demand.
* Trade on Soffex was again dominated by transactions ahead of Friday's expiry.
Dealers said rollovers accounted for the lion's share of Thursday's activities when 15,876 SMI futures were traded, of which 9,615 were January contracts and 6,022 February contracts.
The January SMI rose 35 points to 4,004.0, while the February SMI added 39 points to 4,013. Dealers said there were around 13,000 open SMI contracts.
On the options side, 144,331 contracts changed hands. The call put ratio was 2.10 to one.
